purpose: Define Digest -- monokl's content-identity type -- per docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md §8.4, which supersedes the bare-hex ContentHash(String) of docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 12. A Digest names its algorithm, so a cache entry written today stays distinguishable from one written after an algorithm or width change. FileAnalysis (track #14), the in-memory cache (track #16) and disk persistence (track #17) key on it.
scope: The Digest struct and DigestAlgorithm enum in crates/monokl/src/digest.rs; DigestAlgorithm's text names (as_str and FromStr); Digest::blake3(content) as the one hashing constructor; the textual form `algorithm ":" encoded` produced by Display and accepted by FromStr; the serde wire form, which is that same string, including as a JSON map key; and the parse errors.
non_goals: Computing sha256 digests. DigestAlgorithm::Sha256 exists so a sha256 digest from a third-party harness plugin parses and round-trips (§8.4's boundary table); monokl computes blake3 only, and nothing in monokl needs a sha256 hasher yet.
sha512 or any other OCI-registered algorithm. DigestAlgorithm is exhaustive, exactly §8.4's shape; adding a variant would be done in wisp-contracts and is a breaking change accepted there.
Moving Digest into wisp-contracts. That crate does not exist yet; Digest is shaped to move there unchanged (docs/adr/0002-digest-lives-in-monokl-until-wisp-contracts.md).
FileAnalysis, the cache, and the cache.json format (tracks #14, #16, #17). They reference Digest; their own shapes are not locked here.
Round-trip of Digest-valued fields inside cache.json, and whether a legacy bare-hex hash loads as StaleDiskCache or Json, belong to the track #17 spec, which must carry those criteria.
The cache Tier-1 mtime/size fast-path gap (docs/architecture/cache-architecture.md). It concerns when a digest is compared, not the digest's shape.
Streaming or incremental hashing. Digest::blake3 hashes one byte slice in one call.
An ordering on Digest or DigestAlgorithm. Callers needing a deterministic order sort by to_string().

api_surface.name: DigestAlgorithm
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)] pub enum DigestAlgorithm { Sha256, Blake3 }
api_surface.description: The algorithm half of a digest, exactly §8.4's shape: no #[non_exhaustive], so a downstream crate can match both variants without a wildcard arm.

api_surface.name: DigestAlgorithm::as_str
api_surface.description: Returns "sha256" for Sha256 and "blake3" for Blake3.

api_surface.name: impl FromStr for DigestAlgorithm
api_surface.signature: impl std::str::FromStr for DigestAlgorithm { type Err = DigestParseError; }
api_surface.description: Accepts exactly "sha256" and "blake3", case-sensitive. Any other input is Err(DigestParseError::UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm: <the input> }).

api_surface.name: Digest
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)] pub struct Digest { pub algorithm: DigestAlgorithm, pub bytes: [u8; 32] }

api_surface.name: impl FromStr for Digest
api_surface.signature: impl std::str::FromStr for Digest { type Err = DigestParseError; }
api_surface.description: Parses `algorithm:hex`, splitting at the first `:`. Checks the separator, then the algorithm, then the encoding; never trims.

api_surface.name: DigestParseError
api_surface.signature: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, thiserror::Error)] #[non_exhaustive] pub enum DigestParseError { MissingSeparator, UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm: String }, InvalidEncoding }
api_surface.description: Why a string is not a digest. This spec's own error type, so it stays #[non_exhaustive].

api_surface.name: Serialize / Deserialize for Digest
api_surface.signature: impl Serialize for Digest; impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Digest
api_surface.description: Serializes as the Display string; deserializes from a string through FromStr, so an invalid digest fails to deserialize.
error_conditions: any FromStr error, surfaced as a serde custom error whose message is the DigestParseError Display text

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Digest::blake3(b"") equals Digest { algorithm: DigestAlgorithm::Blake3, bytes: *blake3::hash(b"").as_bytes() }, and its Display output is exactly "blake3:af1349b9f5f9a1a6a0404dea36dcc9499bcb25c9adc112b7cc9a93cae41f3262". Against the official BLAKE3 test vectors (test_vectors/test_vectors.json in BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3; input is the bytes i % 251 for i in 0..input_len; expected value is the first 64 hex characters of `hash`), with input = (0..n).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8): for n = 0 the Display is "blake3:af1349b9f5f9a1a6a0404dea36dcc9499bcb25c9adc112b7cc9a93cae41f3262", for n = 1 it is "blake3:2d3adedff11b61f14c886e35afa036736dcd87a74d27b5c1510225d0f592e213", and for n = 1025 it is "blake3:d00278ae47eb27b34faecf67b4fe263f82d5412916c1ffd97c8cb7fb814b8444".
Digest::blake3 is deterministic: two calls on byte-identical input return equal values, and calls on different inputs b"a" and b"b" return unequal values.

d.to_string().parse::<Digest>() returns Ok(d) for each of these 8 digests: algorithm in {DigestAlgorithm::Blake3, DigestAlgorithm::Sha256} crossed with bytes in {[0x00; 32], [0xff; 32], Digest::blake3(b"monokl").bytes, the bytes 0x00..=0x1f in ascending order}. A property test over arbitrary [u8; 32] crossed with both algorithms asserts the same.

Display writes the algorithm name, one `:`, then two lowercase hex characters per byte: Digest { algorithm: Blake3, bytes: [0xab; 32] } displays as "blake3:" followed by "ab" repeated 32 times, and the same bytes with Sha256 display as "sha256:" followed by "ab" repeated 32 times.
Parsing "af1349b9f5f9a1a6a0404dea36dcc9499bcb25c9adc112b7cc9a93cae41f3262" (a bare 64-character hex string, the old ContentHash form) returns Err(DigestParseError::MissingSeparator).

Parsing each of `md5:`, `sha512:`, `BLAKE3:` and `Sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters returns Err(DigestParseError::UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm }) where algorithm is exactly "md5", "sha512", "BLAKE3" and "Sha256" respectively.

For each prefix P in {"blake3:", "sha256:"}, parsing P followed by each of these returns Err(DigestParseError::InvalidEncoding): 63 lowercase hex characters; 65 lowercase hex characters; nothing (the input is exactly P); 64 characters of which the first is an uppercase `A` and the rest lowercase hex; 64 characters of which the first is `g` and the rest lowercase hex; U+00E9 repeated 32 times (64 bytes, 32 chars); `ab:` followed by 61 lowercase hex characters.

For d = Digest::blake3(b""), serde_json::to_string(&d) is exactly "\"blake3:af1349b9f5f9a1a6a0404dea36dcc9499bcb25c9adc112b7cc9a93cae41f3262\"", and serde_json::from_str, serde_json::from_slice and serde_json::from_reader of that literal each return Ok(d), as does serde_json::from_value(serde_json::to_value(&d)).

serde_json::from_str::<Digest> returns Err (never panics) for the JSON strings "", "af1349b9f5f9a1a6a0404dea36dcc9499bcb25c9adc112b7cc9a93cae41f3262", "md5:" + 64 hex, "BLAKE3:" + 64 hex, "blake3:" + 63 hex, and "blake3:" + 64 uppercase hex; for each, the Err's to_string() contains the Display text of the DigestParseError that FromStr returns for that string (MissingSeparator, MissingSeparator, UnknownAlgorithm { "md5" }, UnknownAlgorithm { "BLAKE3" }, InvalidEncoding, InvalidEncoding). It also returns Err for the JSON values null, 1, true, [] and {}.

Digest and DigestAlgorithm are Copy and usable as HashMap/HashSet keys; equal digests hash equal: a HashSet built from [blake3(b"x"), blake3(b"x"), blake3(b"y")] has len 2, and inserting blake3(b"x") twice into a HashMap leaves len 1 holding the second value.

DigestAlgorithm::Sha256.as_str() is "sha256" and DigestAlgorithm::Blake3.as_str() is "blake3"; for both variants a, a.as_str().parse::<DigestAlgorithm>() == Ok(a); "Blake3".parse::<DigestAlgorithm>() is Err(DigestParseError::UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm: "Blake3" }). A crate outside monokl can match DigestAlgorithm with arms for Sha256 and Blake3 only, no wildcard.

Digest::from_str checks the separator, then the algorithm, then the encoding, and never trims: "" is Err(MissingSeparator); a bare 64-hex string is Err(MissingSeparator); "md5:zz" is Err(UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm: "md5" }); ":" + 64 hex is Err(UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm: "" }); " blake3:" + 64 hex is Err(UnknownAlgorithm { algorithm: " blake3" }); "blake3:" + 64 hex + "\n" is Err(InvalidEncoding).

A HashMap<Digest, u32> of {blake3(b"a"): 1, blake3(b"b"): 2} serializes to a JSON object whose keys are exactly blake3(b"a").to_string() and blake3(b"b").to_string(), and deserializes back to an equal map. serde_json::from_str::<HashMap<Digest, u32>>(r#"{"deadbeef":1}"#) returns Err.
Digest { algorithm: Blake3, bytes: [0xab; 32] } != Digest { algorithm: Sha256, bytes: [0xab; 32] }, their Display strings differ, and a HashSet containing both has len 2.

linked_research: docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md §8.4 and §14; docs/adr/0002-digest-lives-in-monokl-until-wisp-contracts.md; docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md §16 (declare-as-implemented: blake3 and proptest are listed because code uses them) and §18 (determinism: no ordering is defined on Digest, so ordered output sorts by the text form); OCI image-spec descriptor digest grammar; BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3 test_vectors/test_vectors.json; docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Section 12 (superseded). No requirement@1 named REQ-011 exists; this spec is grounded in Part 8 §8.4/§14 and ADR 0002.
revision_note:
2026-10-23 correction: replaced ContentHash(String) with Digest per Part 8 §8.4, which supersedes it (§14). An unprefixed hash is unmigratable, and the old spec explicitly declined deserialize-time validation; Digest validates on parse and deserialize. The earlier ContentHash criteria are withdrawn, not carried over.
2026-10-23: Retroactive gate: verifier/auditor findings applied.
reasoning: Shape, grammar and the lowercase rule come straight from §8.4; DigestAlgorithm drops #[non_exhaustive] so the shape is exactly §8.4's, as ADR 0002 claims. Choices this spec makes that §8.4 leaves open: a single blake3 constructor (sha256 is parse-only, non_goals); DigestAlgorithm::as_str/FromStr as the one place algorithm names live; serde goes through the Display/FromStr string so the wire form, the text form and the map-key form cannot drift; a second `:` is InvalidEncoding rather than a separate variant, since parsing splits at the first `:` and the encoded part is what is malformed; parse order is separator, algorithm, encoding so the error names the first thing wrong. AC-010 asserts only the positive Copy/Eq/Hash contract; the absence of PartialOrd/Ord/Default is not asserted because it cannot be tested without a compile-fail harness, and callers needing deterministic order sort by to_string(). Digest lives in monokl until wisp-contracts exists (ADR 0002).
